nodes.label: MariaDB 10.4.32
nodes.rationale: 10.4.32-MariaDB is the supported engine. The baseline, its snapshot and the tests are taken on that version. Other MariaDB or MySQL versions report types, defaults and view text differently, so flask db-adopt will warn about differences that come only from the server. The MySQL 8.2 dumps in backups are not the schema source: they use utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, which MariaDB 10.4 does not have. Regenerate the baseline with the XAMPP MariaDB mysqldump, not the MySQL client on PATH, because phpMyAdmin drops CHECK constraints.

nodes.label: Alembic schema ownership
nodes.rationale: Alembic, through Flask-Migrate, owns the schema. The application still reads and writes rows with raw SQL in models/db.py and has no ORM models, so autogenerate is disabled: it would only propose dropping every table. The app never runs DDL itself. Never edit a revision once any database has been upgraded or stamped with it. Always write downgrade. Test a new revision on a copy before college_timetable_db. Hand-written revisions only.

nodes.label: 0001_baseline
nodes.rationale: Creates college_timetable_db: 54 tables and 10 views. migrations/_archive kept a first attempt that reused the revision id 0001_baseline, so a database stamped by that old attempt would look adopted when it is not. college_timetable_db was adopted and upgraded to 0007 on 8 Nov 2026; 0008 had not been applied yet.

nodes.label: 0007_lecture_sessions
nodes.rationale: Creates lecture_sessions and attendance_excuses and adds nullable attendance.session_id with a RESTRICT foreign key. After upgrading a database that already has attendance rows, backfill sessions before 0008.

nodes.label: 0008_attendance_views
nodes.rationale: Makes attendance.session_id NOT NULL and drops attendance_summary and student_overall_attendance, which no code reads. It refuses to run while any attendance row has no session_id. Downgrade makes the column nullable again and recreates the views from the baseline text.

nodes.label: 0009_worker_claims
nodes.rationale: Adds locked_by and heartbeat_at to processed_reports and timetable_jobs so a restart or a second worker requeues only rows whose heartbeat is older than JOB_STALE_SECONDS.

nodes.label: Shared job-claim columns
nodes.rationale: A worker writes its id when it claims a row and refreshes the heartbeat on every progress update. The same locked_by and heartbeat_at columns are on processed_reports, timetable_jobs, notifications and webhook_deliveries, so one restart rule covers exports, generation, mail and webhooks.

nodes.label: 0010_face_safeguards
nodes.rationale: Creates face_consents and face_recognition_audit. Face templates themselves are encrypted in place by the application; this revision changes no template columns.

nodes.label: 0011_notifications
nodes.rationale: Creates the notifications outbox and the single-row notification_settings table, including a Fernet-encrypted SMTP password and the shared claim columns.

nodes.label: 0012_lab_batches
nodes.rationale: Creates lab_batch_groups and lab_batch_members and adds nullable timetable.lab_batch_group_id. Null means a whole-division slot. The foreign key is ON DELETE SET NULL.

nodes.label: 0013_integrations
nodes.rationale: Creates api_keys, webhook_endpoints, webhook_deliveries, sso_settings and sso_identities. Webhook secrets and the SSO client secret are Fernet-encrypted.

nodes.label: 0014_institutions
nodes.rationale: Several colleges in one tenant. Backfill inserts organization and institution 1 before the foreign keys, leaves existing departments and rooms there, and gives every non-student user a primary membership. Downgrade drops the columns and tables, so which college owned what is lost. The DEFAULT 1 is deliberate so inserts that do not name an institution still land in the first one.

nodes.label: 0015_capabilities
nodes.rationale: One row per optional feature. A missing row means the registry default. A missing table means every optional feature is off. Rows are written only from Settings, Capabilities.

nodes.label: 0016_timetable_preferences
nodes.rationale: Creates faculty_preferences and timetable_rules. Both are read only when the timetable_preferences capability is on.

nodes.label: 0017_timetable_versions
nodes.rationale: Draft rows carry is_active 0 so readers that filter active rows are unaffected. Null version_id means a row written before versions or while the capability is off. Downgrade turns every draft row into an ordinary retired row.

nodes.label: 0018_bookings
nodes.rationale: A room reserved for an event, exam, maintenance or external use. Only approved rows block a room, and only while the bookings capability is on.

nodes.label: 0019_academic_calendar
nodes.rationale: Adds institution, optional semester and kind to the baseline academic_terms table, and adds calendar to lecture_sessions.cancel_reason. Read only while capability academic_terms is on. Downgrade rewrites any calendar reason to other. The table itself stays.

nodes.label: 0020_syllabus
nodes.rationale: Creates syllabus_units and lesson_logs. Read and written only while capability syllabus is on.

nodes.label: 0021_assessment
nodes.rationale: Creates assessment components, marks, course outcomes, program outcomes, co_po_map and component_co_map. A mark is shown to the student only after the component is locked. Read and written only while capability assessments is on.

nodes.label: 0022_exam_schedule
nodes.rationale: Creates exams, exam sessions, cohorts, rooms, seats and invigilation duties. A saved session occupies its rooms on the booking ledger while bookings is on. Read and written only while capability exams is on.

nodes.label: flask db-adopt
nodes.rationale: An existing database already has the baseline tables, so flask db upgrade from nothing would fail. db-adopt compares information_schema to the baseline snapshot inside a read-only transaction and, if nothing differs and the database is unstamped, stamps 0001_baseline and nothing else. Do not edit the baseline to make a database fit. Check alembic_version before adopting, because the archived baseline reused that revision id.

nodes.label: flask seed run
nodes.rationale: Seeders only add rows. They never update or delete one, so a role, permission or branding value a college has changed stays. Role-permission defaults are one-time grants recorded in seed_history, so a permission a college removed stays removed. An existing database that already has role permissions is not granted the rest until flask seed run --apply-role-defaults. A later default carries a higher since version and is granted once. Super Admin passes every permission check whatever its rows say; it is mapped to every permission only so the role editor shows it complete. There are no default accounts or passwords.

nodes.label: flask admin create-superadmin
nodes.rationale: The only way the first account is made, and it needs the Super Admin role that seed run inserts. The password is stored as a werkzeug hash. The audit entry never includes the password or hash. --force only adds another account; it never changes an existing one.

nodes.label: Time-based sign-in lock
nodes.rationale: Five failures within fifteen minutes set locked_until fifteen minutes ahead by the database clock. The lock ends by itself. Every failed sign-in form POST answers the same 401 whether the username is unknown, the password is wrong, or the account is locked or inactive, and an unknown username still runs one password hash. status locked remains a manual lock, but sign-in no longer sets it. Rows locked that way before 0006 stay locked until an admin unlocks them. Super Admin accounts get the same temporary lock.

nodes.label: Sign-in rate limits
nodes.rationale: Counters live in rate_limit_counters. Behind a reverse proxy, TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT must equal the real number of proxies so ProxyFix reads the client from X-Forwarded-For. It is 0 by default, and then the headers are ignored. Never set it higher than the real number of proxies: a client could then choose its own address.

nodes.label: Account authority
nodes.rationale: roles.hierarchy_level orders roles; smaller is more senior. An actor manages only accounts whose role level is larger than their own, and can only give a role they could manage. Only a Super Admin manages a Super Admin, and the last active Super Admin cannot be deactivated or demoted. Nobody deactivates their own account. Granting or revoking a user's permissions needs users_manage_permissions, held by no role but Super Admin by default, and only permissions the actor holds. Checks read the actor's role from the database and apply to the JSON API and the legacy admin routes.

nodes.label: Attendance calculation service
nodes.rationale: Every percentage a screen or export shows comes from services/attendance_calc.py, which loads students, slots, lecture_sessions, marks and excuses and hands them to the pure attendance_calc package. The denominator is held lectures the student was rostered for. A mark the teacher saved always counts even outside that roster. Cancelled lectures, holidays and not_marked lectures are not counted. Late counts as present. An excused absence leaves the denominator. Nothing countable is null, shown as a dash, not 0. Overall and Theory/Practical figures are pooled. ATTENDANCE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT defaults to 75 and can be overridden for one call.

nodes.label: flask attendance close-day
nodes.rationale: For each active slot that meets that weekday, close-day inserts not_marked unless a session already exists, the date is a holiday, or the date is outside the slot's semester. It refuses today and future dates. It also completes the roster of held sessions a face device recorded: each roster student without a mark gets Absent, while teacher-marked sessions stay unrecorded. The worker closes the last 7 days so a day missed while the app was down is still closed. Deleting a slot that has sessions is refused; the admin delete retires the slot so the history stays.

nodes.label: flask attendance backfill-sessions
nodes.rationale: Creates one held session with source backfill for every timetable and date that has attendance rows but no session, and links those rows. It never invents unmarked lectures. It only reports anomalies. Marks on a cancelled session stay unlinked until they are deleted or the session is restored. It is the one command that runs on a database at 0007 or later; every other command needs head. The deployment order when 0008 stops is upgrade, backfill, upgrade.

nodes.label: Startup schema check
nodes.rationale: When REQUIRE_MIGRATED_DB is true, startup compares alembic_version with the newest revision. If the database is behind, unstamped, unknown or unreachable, /health returns 503. Other routes are not blocked. /health checks again on every call, so it returns 200 as soon as the database is upgraded, without a restart. Flask CLI commands other than flask run start no background work and skip this check.

nodes.label: Test database name guard
nodes.rationale: The suite reads database settings only from .env.test, never .env, and refuses to run unless the name starts with college_timetable_ci_ and ends in _test. It refuses college_timetable_db and college_timetable_db_test by name so tests cannot touch the live database. The access-data dump must not include users, students, faculty or other personal data.

nodes.label: Permission canon
nodes.rationale: tests/unit/test_permission_canon.py scans every permission check and fails if the code checks a name that is not in the canon, if a permission marked enforced is not checked anywhere, or if a permission marked not enforced is outside its allowlist of 24.

nodes.label: Unenforced permissions
nodes.rationale: 24 permissions that no code checks still exist on installed databases and are shown in the role editor, where granting or removing them does nothing. Do not delete the rows. Either add the check or hide them, then change enforced and update the allowlist.

nodes.label: Mixed collations
nodes.rationale: academic_terms and timetable_jobs use utf8mb4_general_ci; the other 52 baseline tables use utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Left as is because changing a collation can break joins and comparisons. A later fix belongs in its own revision, tested on a copy.

nodes.label: test_migration_baseline.py
nodes.rationale: Builds one scratch database with the migrations and one from the structure dump, and checks that their information_schema matches, that db-adopt refuses a changed schema without writing, and that 0002 is idempotent. It never connects to the live database.

nodes.label: Open lab-batch audit xfail
nodes.rationale: test_audit_regressions.py treats as still open the bug that a practical cannot be limited to a lab batch because there are no lab sub-batch tables, and points at DESIGN_LAB_BATCHES.md. That design says revision 0012 implemented the tables.

hyperedges.label: Transactional outbox with shared job claims
